subject: OSCE Procedures
topic: A. Administration of drugs - Administration of dangerous drugs
question: Describe the procedure for administering controlled/dangerous drugs
answer: 1. Verify prescription and controlled drug order. 2. Check patient identity with two identifiers. 3. Count controlled drugs with another nurse (witness). 4. Document on controlled drug register: date, time, patient name, drug name, dose, signature of administering nurse and witness. 5. Prepare medication using aseptic technique. 6. Administer to patient. 7. Observe for effects/side effects. 8. Document administration in patient record. 9. Return and properly store remaining stock. 10. Count remaining stock with witness. 11. Report discrepancies immediately.

subject: OSCE Procedures
topic: A. Administration of drugs - Application of eye ointment
question: How do you apply eye ointment correctly?
answer: 1. Verify order, perform hand hygiene. 2. Gather equipment: eye ointment, gloves, tissue. 3. Identify patient, explain procedure. 4. Position patient sitting or lying with head tilted back. 5. Remove contact lenses if present. 6. Remove cap, avoid touching tube tip. 7. Gently pull down lower lid to create conjunctival sac. 8. Ask patient to look up. 9. Apply thin ribbon of ointment along inner edge of lower lid from inner to outer canthus. 10. Release lid, ask patient to close eyes gently and roll eyes. 11. Remove excess ointment from lids. 12. Advise patient of temporary blurred vision. 13. Document.

subject: OSCE Procedures
topic: A. Administration of drugs - Intravenous infusion
question: Describe the procedure for setting up and monitoring intravenous infusion
answer: 1. Verify order for fluid type, rate, duration. 2. Perform hand hygiene, gather equipment: prescribed IV fluid, administration set, IV pole, cannula, dressing, tourniquet, antiseptic. 3. Check fluid for expiration, clarity, leaks. 4. Prime administration set: close roller clamp, spike bag, squeeze drip chamber to fill halfway, open clamp slowly to remove air. 5. Identify patient, explain procedure. 6. Select vein, apply tourniquet. 7. Clean site. 8. Insert cannula, secure. 9. Connect primed tubing, adjust rate (drops/min = volume × drop factor ÷ time in minutes). 10. Label with date/time/signature. 11. Monitor: site for infiltration/phlebitis, rate accuracy, patient response. 12. Document fluid intake, observations.

subject: OSCE Procedures
topic: A. Administration of drugs - Oral medication administration
question: Describe the procedure for administering oral medications
answer: 1. Verify medication order (MAR/eMAR). 2. Perform hand hygiene. 3. Gather medications, check against MAR (Right Drug). 4. Check expiration dates. 5. Identify patient using two identifiers (Right Patient). 6. Explain procedure to patient. 7. Verify allergies. 8. Prepare medications: pour tablets into cap, crush if needed (check if appropriate), cut if scored. 9. Administer with adequate fluid (unless NPO). 10. Stay until medication is swallowed. 11. Observe for adverse effects. 12. Document administration (time, dose, route). 13. Record effectiveness if PRN (pain, nausea).

subject: OSCE Procedures
topic: B. Bed making procedures - Occupied bed making
question: How do you make an occupied bed?
answer: 1. Gather linen: bottom sheet, top sheet, pillowcases, drawsheet, blanket. 2. Perform hand hygiene, explain procedure to patient. 3. Lower side rail on working side, raise bed to comfortable height. 4. Loosen top linen. 5. Cover patient with bath blanket, remove top linen. 6. Position patient on far side, assist to maintain position. 7. Fan-fold soiled linen toward patient. 8. Place clean bottom sheet, fan-fold toward patient. 9. Tuck and miter corner on working side. 10. Place drawsheet, tuck securely. 11. Log-roll patient to clean side. 12. Move to other side, remove soiled linen. 13. Pull clean linen through, tuck and miter. 14. Place clean top sheet and blanket, remove bath blanket. 15. Change pillowcases. 16. Position patient comfortably, raise side rails as needed. 17. Dispose of soiled linen properly.

subject: OSCE Procedures
topic: B. Bed making procedures - Cardiac bed
question: Describe how to prepare a cardiac bed
answer: 1. Gather linen: bottom sheet, top sheet, blanket, pillowcases, extra pillows (4-6), backrest. 2. Position bed in high Fowler's or semi-Fowler's. 3. Place bottom sheet as usual. 4. Place drawsheet if needed. 5. Place backrest at head of bed. 6. Arrange pillows to support back, shoulders, and arms. 7. Place overbed table within reach for patient to lean on. 8. Fold top linen in fan pleats at foot of bed. 9. Keep call bell within reach. 10. Have oxygen and suction equipment ready. 11. Place cardiac table/stand nearby for emergency equipment. 12. Document preparation.

subject: OSCE Procedures
topic: G. Wound care - Incision and drainage of abscess
question: Describe the nurse's role in incision and drainage of abscess
answer: Pre-procedure: 1. Verify consent. 2. Assess abscess: size, location, fluctuance. 3. Prepare sterile tray with scalpel, forceps, gauze, drain material. 4. Position patient for optimal access. 5. Clean site with antiseptic. Intra-procedure (assisting): 1. Support patient during procedure. 2. Pass instruments as needed. 3. Observe for bleeding/pain. 4. Receive specimen for culture if needed. Post-procedure: 1. Pack wound if indicated (iodoform gauze). 2. Apply sterile dressing. 3. Monitor vital signs. 4. Assess pain and administer analgesics. 5. Instruct patient on wound care, signs of infection. 6. Document procedure, findings, patient tolerance. 7. Arrange follow-up for pack removal.

subject: OSCE Procedures
topic: G. Wound care - Suturing of wounds
question: Describe the nurse's role in wound suturing
answer: Assisting role: 1. Verify consent and tetanus status. 2. Prepare sterile suture set (needle holder, forceps, scissors, suture material). 3. Clean wound with antiseptic, drape. 4. Pass instruments to practitioner. 5. Provide adequate lighting. 6. Observe patient for pain, tolerance. 7. After suturing: clean area, apply dressing. 8. Provide wound care instructions: keep clean and dry, signs of infection, when to return for suture removal. 9. Document: wound description, number of sutures, location, patient tolerance. In some settings/emergencies, nurses may perform simple suturing after training and per protocol.

subject: OSCE Procedures
topic: E. Gastrointestinal procedures and Care - Gastric aspiration and lavage
question: Describe gastric aspiration and lavage procedure
answer: Indications: Drug overdose, poisoning, gastric bleeding, pre-operative. Equipment: Large-bore NG tube (28-36 Fr), lubricant, emesis basin, 50ml syringe, water-soluble lubricant, stethoscope, tape, suction apparatus, lavage solution (normal saline). Procedure: 1. Assess airway, position patient left lateral Trendelenburg. 2. Measure tube from nose to earlobe to xiphoid process, mark. 3. Lubricate tip, insert gently through nostril. 4. Advance as patient swallows. 5. Verify placement: aspirate gastric contents, auscultate air insufflation, pH testing. 6. Aspirate stomach contents (save specimen if needed). 7. Instill 200-300ml lavage fluid, aspirate back. 8. Repeat until clear. 9. Remove tube or leave for subsequent drainage. 10. Monitor patient throughout. 11. Document: amount and character of aspirate, patient tolerance.

subject: OSCE Procedures
topic: E. Gastrointestinal procedures and Care - Enema administration
question: Describe the procedure for administering an enema
answer: Indications: Constipation, bowel preparation, elimination of flatus. Types: Cleansing (soap suds), retention (oil, medication), return flow (Harris flush). Equipment: Enema bag/tube, solution (warmed to 40-43°C), lubricant, bedpan, waterproof pad. Procedure: 1. Verify order, explain procedure. 2. Provide privacy, position patient left Sims' position. 3. Prime tubing to remove air. 4. Lubricate tip. 5. Insert tip gently 7-10cm (adults) toward umbilicus. 6. Hang bag 30-45cm above anus. 7. Administer slowly over 5-10 minutes. 8. Clamp tubing, remove gently. 9. Encourage retention (5-15 minutes for cleansing, longer for retention). 10. Assist to bedpan or bathroom. 11. Observe results. 12. Document: type, amount, result, patient tolerance.

subject: OSCE Procedures
topic: F. Care of the urinary system and procedures - Urinary catheterization (female)
question: Describe female urinary catheterization procedure
answer: Indications: Retention, accurate output monitoring, pre-operative, specimen collection. Equipment: Sterile catheter kit (14-16 Fr Foley), antiseptic solution, lubricant, gloves, sterile drapes, drainage bag, 5-10ml sterile water for balloon. Procedure: 1. Verify order, explain to patient. 2. Provide privacy, position dorsal recumbent with knees flexed. 3. Perform hand hygiene, open sterile kit using aseptic technique. 4. Don sterile gloves. 5. Drape patient with sterile fenestrated drape. 6. Clean perineal area: labia majora → minora → meatus (front to back). 7. Lubricate catheter tip. 8. Separate labia with non-dominant hand (now contaminated). 9. Insert catheter gently 5-7cm until urine flows. 10. Inflate balloon with sterile water (5-10ml). 11. Gently pull back until resistance. 12. Connect to drainage bag. 13. Secure catheter to thigh. 14. Document: size, amount inserted, balloon volume, urine characteristics, patient tolerance.

subject: OSCE Procedures
topic: F. Care of the urinary system and procedures - Bladder washout (irrigation)
question: Describe bladder washout/irrigation procedure
answer: Indications: Remove clots, debris; maintain patency; instill medication. Equipment: Sterile irrigation set, sterile normal saline (warmed), sterile syringe (30-50ml), sterile basin, sterile gloves. Procedure: 1. Verify order. 2. Perform hand hygiene, don sterile gloves. 3. Drain bladder completely via catheter. 4. Disconnect catheter from drainage bag (maintain sterility). 5. Fill syringe with 30-50ml sterile normal saline. 6. Instill gently into catheter. 7. Allow to drain back by gravity or gently aspirate. 8. Repeat until returns are clear. 9. Reconnect to drainage bag. 10. Document: amount used, characteristics of returns, patient tolerance. Closed irrigation: Use three-way catheter with continuous irrigation via tubing.

subject: OSCE Procedures
topic: J. Special care/specific interventions - Oxygen administration
question: Describe oxygen administration methods and nursing considerations
answer: Methods: 1. Nasal cannula: 1-6 L/min (24-44% FiO2). 2. Simple face mask: 5-8 L/min (40-60%). 3. Non-rebreather mask: 10-15 L/min (80-95%). 4. Venturi mask: precise FiO2 (24-50%) at specific flow rates. 5. Tracheostomy collar. Procedure: 1. Assess respiratory status (rate, depth, O2 saturation, ABGs). 2. Verify order (method, flow rate, FiO2). 3. Assemble equipment, attach to flow meter. 4. Explain to patient. 5. Apply device comfortably. 6. Adjust to prescribed settings. 7. Monitor response: vital signs, O2 saturation, level of consciousness. 8. Assess for complications: oxygen toxicity, CO2 narcosis, drying of mucous membranes (humidify if >4 L/min). 9. Document: method, flow rate, FiO2, patient response.

subject: OSCE Procedures
topic: J. Special care/specific interventions - Tracheostomy care
question: Describe tracheostomy care procedure
answer: Equipment: Sterile tracheostomy cleaning kit, sterile gloves, sterile normal saline, hydrogen peroxide (diluted), sterile suction kit, tracheostomy ties, inner cannula (disposable or reusable). Frequency: Every 8 hours and PRN. Procedure: 1. Explain procedure to patient. 2. Perform hand hygiene. 3. Suction tracheostomy if needed. 4. Remove soiled dressing, clean around stoma with sterile saline. 5. Remove inner cannula: if disposable, replace with new; if reusable, clean with peroxide/saline, rinse thoroughly, dry, reinsert. 6. Change tracheostomy ties: secure new ties before removing old ones. 7. Place sterile dressing around stoma. 8. Assess stoma for redness, exudate. 9. Monitor respiratory status. 10. Document procedure, findings, patient tolerance. Emergency equipment: Extra tracheostomy tube, obturator, oxygen, suction at bedside.

subject: OSCE Procedures
topic: J. Special care/specific interventions - Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR)
question: Describe adult CPR procedure (BLS)
answer: Follow current AHA/ERC guidelines: 1. Assess scene safety. 2. Check responsiveness: tap and shout. 3. If unresponsive, activate emergency response system, get AED. 4. Check breathing and pulse simultaneously (≤10 seconds). 5. If no pulse or not sure, start CPR. 6. Compression: heel of hand on lower half of sternum, other hand on top, interlock fingers. 7. Depth: 5-6cm (2-2.4 inches). 8. Rate: 100-120/min. 9. Allow full chest recoil. 10. 30 compressions : 2 ventilations (2-person: 15:2 if advanced airway). 11. Ventilations: open airway (head tilt-chin lift), give breath over 1 second, observe chest rise. 12. Minimize interruptions (<10 seconds). 13. Rotate compressors every 2 minutes. 14. Use AED as soon as available: follow prompts. 15. Continue until ROSC or medical help takes over.

subject: OSCE Procedures
topic: J. Special care/specific interventions - Last respect to the dead (Last offices)
question: Describe the procedure for last offices (care of the deceased)
answer: Purpose: Prepare body for viewing, maintain dignity, respect cultural/religious practices. Procedure: 1. Confirm death with medical officer. 2. Support family, allow them time with deceased according to culture. 3. Obtain consent for post-mortem if needed. 4. Wear gloves and gown. 5. Close patient's eyes gently. 6. Remove tubes, lines, catheters (check policy). 7. Clean body thoroughly. 8. Pack orifices with absorbent material if needed. 9. Dress in clean gown or preferred clothing. 10. Position body supine, arms at sides or across abdomen, head on pillow. 11. Replace dentures if culturally appropriate. 12. Place identification tags: wrist, ankle, body bag. 13. Collect belongings, document. 14. Place in body bag, transfer to mortuary. 15. Provide emotional support to family. 16. Document procedure, time, notifications. 17. Follow facility policy for valuables and belongings.

subject: OSCE Procedures
topic: H. Clinical Observations/diagnostic procedures - Vital signs observation
question: Describe assessment and measurement of vital signs
answer: Temperature: Routes: oral (35.5-37.5°C), axillary (34.7-37.3°C), rectal (36.6-38.0°C), tympanic, temporal. Normal range 36.5-37.5°C. Pulse: Rate (60-100/min adults), rhythm, volume. Palpate radial, carotid, apical. Respiration: Rate (12-20/min adults), depth, rhythm, effort. Blood Pressure: Systolic (100-120 mmHg), diastolic (60-80 mmHg). Method: patient seated/lying, arm at heart level, appropriate cuff size. Procedure: 1. Explain procedure. 2. Ensure patient rested. 3. Measure in consistent manner. 4. Record accurately. 5. Report abnormalities. Oxygen saturation (SpO2): Normal >95%. Pain assessment: 0-10 scale, PQRST (Provokes, Quality, Radiates, Severity, Time).

subject: OSCE Procedures
topic: H. Clinical Observations/diagnostic procedures - Lumbar puncture
question: Describe the nurse's role in lumbar puncture
answer: Pre-procedure: 1. Verify consent, check coagulation studies. 2. Explain procedure to patient. 3. Position patient: lateral recumbent (fetal position) or sitting leaning forward. 4. Prepare sterile lumbar puncture tray. 5. Ensure emergency equipment available. Intra-procedure: 1. Assist patient maintain position. 2. Support and reassure patient. 3. Pass instruments as needed. 4. Observe for adverse reactions (vagal response). 5. Receive specimens (CSF) for labs. Post-procedure: 1. Apply small dressing. 2. Instruct patient to lie flat for 4-6 hours (prevent post-dural headache). 3. Encourage fluids. 4. Monitor vital signs, neurological status. 5. Assess for headache, bleeding, infection. 6. Document procedure, specimens sent, patient tolerance.

subject: OSCE Procedures
topic: H. Clinical Observations/diagnostic procedures - Urine testing
question: Describe urine testing procedures
answer: Types: Urinalysis (dipstick), specific gravity, microscopic, culture. Dipstick: 1. Collect fresh specimen (midstream clean catch preferred). 2. Dip strip completely, remove immediately. 3. Hold edge to remove excess. 4. Read at specified time for each parameter. 5. Compare to color chart. Parameters: pH (4.5-8), Specific gravity (1.005-1.030), Protein, Glucose, Ketones, Blood, Bilirubin, Urobilinogen, Nitrite, Leukocyte esterase. Specific gravity: Use urinometer. Fill cylinder, float urinometer, read at meniscus. Culture: Clean catch midstream, sterile container. Document: Color, clarity, odor, results, send to lab if indicated.

subject: OSCE Procedures
topic: D. Patient hygiene - Bathing a baby
question: Describe infant bathing procedure
answer: Equipment: Baby bath tub, warm water (37-38°C), mild baby soap, soft washcloth, hooded towel, clean diaper, clothes, cotton balls. Safety: Never leave infant unattended. Procedure: 1. Gather supplies, ensure room warm. 2. Fill tub with 2-3 inches water. 3. Test water temperature (wrist/elbow). 4. Undress infant except diaper. 5. Wrap in towel, clean face first: eyes (inner to outer) with plain water. 6. Wash scalp with water, shampoo if needed. 7. Remove diaper, place in tub supporting head and neck. 8. Wash front to back, paying attention to creases. 9. Rinse thoroughly. 10. Lift out, wrap in hooded towel. 11. Pat dry, apply diaper cream if needed. 12. Diaper and dress. 13. Clean bath equipment. 14. Document.

subject: OSCE Procedures
topic: D. Patient hygiene - Hand hygiene
question: Describe proper hand hygiene technique
answer: Handwashing (soap and water): 1. Remove jewelry. 2. Wet hands with running water. 3. Apply soap. 4. Rub hands palm to palm. 5. Right palm over left dorsum and vice versa. 6. Palm to palm with fingers interlaced. 7. Backs of fingers to opposing palms. 8. Rotational rubbing of thumbs. 9. Rotational rubbing of fingertips into palms. 10. Rinse thoroughly. 11. Dry with single-use towel. 12. Use towel to turn off faucet. Duration: 40-60 seconds. Alcohol-based hand rub: 1. Apply product to palm. 2. Rub hands together covering all surfaces. 3. Continue until dry. Duration: 20-30 seconds. Indications: Before/after patient contact, before aseptic tasks, after body fluid exposure, after touching patient surroundings.

subject: OSCE Procedures
topic: C. Eye and Ear Procedures - Eye irrigation
question: Describe eye irrigation procedure
answer: Indications: Chemical exposure, debris removal, infection. Equipment: Sterile irrigation solution (normal saline), sterile basin, sterile eye irrigating syringe/IV tubing with catheter, waterproof pad, towels. Procedure: 1. Verify order, explain to patient. 2. Position patient sitting or lying with head tilted toward affected side. 3. Place waterproof pad and basin to collect runoff. 4. Perform hand hygiene, don gloves. 5. Remove contact lenses if present. 6. Gently retract eyelids with thumb and forefinger. 7. Direct irrigation stream from inner canthus to outer canthus. 8. Irrigate with gentle pressure, avoid direct stream onto cornea. 9. Continue until solution runs clear or ordered amount used. 10. Dry surrounding skin. 11. Assess eye for redness, injury. 12. Document: solution used, amount, patient response, eye appearance.

subject: OSCE Procedures
topic: K. Others - Patient counseling
question: Describe the principles of patient counseling
answer: Definition: Therapeutic communication to help patient make informed decisions and cope with health issues. Principles: 1. Establish therapeutic relationship. 2. Ensure privacy and confidentiality. 3. Active listening. 4. Empathy and non-judgmental attitude. 5. Use open-ended questions. 6. Assess patient knowledge and readiness. 7. Provide accurate, understandable information. 8. Explore feelings and concerns. 9. Support patient autonomy and decision-making. 10. Set realistic goals. 11. Summarize and verify understanding. 12. Document key points. Areas: Pre-operative, discharge planning, lifestyle changes, medication adherence, coping with chronic illness, family planning, grief counseling.

subject: OSCE Procedures
topic: K. Others - Ward report writing
question: Describe the components of effective nursing ward report
answer: Purpose: Communicate patient status between shifts. Types: Verbal (handover), written (nursing notes, Kardex). Components: 1. Patient identification. 2. Diagnosis and relevant history. 3. Vital signs and trends. 4. Significant events during shift. 5. Treatments and medications given. 6. Pending investigations/results. 7. Patient responses to interventions. 8. Consultations and referrals. 9. Specific instructions for next shift. 10. Safety concerns. Format: SBAR (Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation). Guidelines: Objective, accurate, concise, timely, legible, signed with designation. Avoid: Opinions, judgments, vague statements. Document immediately after care.
